title: In 40 freely moving C. elegans, gap junctions predict pairwise co-activity after controls for neurite contact, soma distance and per-neuron effects; chemical synapse weight does not
abstract: Question: in C. elegans, does connectome structure predict which neurons are co-active, after we remove per-neuron effects? Does the number of inputs to a neuron predict its coupling to the population? A mouse V1 study in this campaign found that a per-neuron effect explained the full pair-level link. Approach: we used whole-brain calcium activity of NeuroPAL-identified neurons in 40 freely moving animals (Atanas, Kim et al. 2023; about 16 min each). We compared it with the Cook 2019 hermaphrodite connectome and the Witvliet 2021 adult Datasets 7 and 8. Outcome: absolute across-animal mean Fisher z of 7,872 neuron pairs, for raw traces, behaviour-removed traces and first differences. Controls: homologous pair, same ganglion, atlas soma distance, a fixed effect for each neuron, and Witvliet neurite contact area. Inference: QAP permutation (2,000) and per-animal models. Results: gap junction weight predicts co-activity after all controls (partial r 0.19, QAP z 14.5, Holm p 0.002; 40 of 40 animals positive). The result repeats with both Witvliet connectomes (0.22, 0.19) and for behaviour-removed traces (0.22). Chemical synapse weight predicts co-activity before controls (0.16), but after neurite contact it is near zero (0.04 Cook; -0.02 to -0.05 Witvliet). Shared chemical input gives a small robust effect (0.06-0.11). Thus, unlike mouse V1, per-neuron effects do not explain the pair-level link. Cell level: the pre-specified in-degree test is not significant after neuron-type control (partial Spearman 0.03, p 0.71). Chemical input weight predicts behaviour-removed population communality after type control (0.27-0.35 in three connectomes, Holm p 0.0004-0.009). Limitations: connectomes and activity come from different animals; contact data come from one animal and nerve-ring neurons only; atlas soma distance cannot exclude all imaging crosstalk; correlations are not causal; one lab and one behavioural condition.

display.caption: Partial correlation of four structure measures with pair co-activity as controls are added (Cook connectome, 7,872 pairs). Gap junctions keep their link after neurite contact is controlled. Chemical weight does not.
A: per-animal partial correlations with all controls (40 animals). B: the same test with the Cook and two Witvliet connectomes.
Cell level: in-degree and input weight against population communality. Neuron type explains most of the in-degree effect; input weight keeps a link for behaviour-removed activity.

citations.reason: We test its two V1 Deep Dive results in C. elegans. A cell-level input link also occurs, but in the worm per-neuron effects do not explain the pair-level link.
